text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some 2,400 people were killed and thousands more were injured by a powerful earthquake which flattened villages in eastern Iran.
- Opposition wards in Potong Pasir and Hougang will form standalone Community Development Councils by December and will receive the government benefits and support they are entitled to.

- Australia's A$3.3 billion overseas student industry may have been badly damaged by the race debate sparked by rightwing MP Pauline Hanson's call to limit Asian immigrants, Education Minister Amanda Vanstone said.

- A consortium of Singapore companies has virtually withdrawn from the Singapore $640 million Bangalore airport project following Indian government insistence on building the facility under a Build-Own-Transfer scheme.
- Shangri-La's Rasa Sentosa Resort is in the red for the fourth consecutive year despite its popularity among Singaporeans as a holiday destination.
- U.S. based Intel Corp has confirmed there is a flaw in its Pentium Pro and Pentium II chips and is offering software to correct the bug.

- Four listed companies in Singapore and Malaysia are said to be involved in takeover deals this week worth between S$1.5-$2.5 billion. Some of the personalities involved are relaties of Indonesian President Suharto and Malaysian Premier Mahathir Mohamad.
- Malaysia's Proton car maker DRB-Hicom will manufacture car parts in Indonesia in a S$46 million joint venture project with the country's national carmaker PT Timor.

- The steep slide of the U.S. dollar against the yen and other leading currencies could accelerate this week, spurred by fears of central bank intervention and a possible early rise in Japanese official interest rates.
- Health care and property group Parkway Holdings' network of hospitals is rapidly expanding with the expected opening of Gleneagles Medan in Indonesia and Duncan Gleneagles in India.
- The Standard P&I Club has given the nod by local authorities to set up the first protection and indemnity insurance club in Singapore.
- Business Focus Sdn Bhd, the umbrella holding company of Malaysian entrepreneur Amin Shah Omar, said it has plans to acquire a U.S. shipyard.
